claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me the **name of your child or children** that you'd like me to assess for eligibility?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex. He's just turned 18 and is still living at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few questions to assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit.

First, could you tell me: **Is Alex in full-time education or undertaking an approved training course?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's still in college doing his A-levels. He started them last year and he's got another year to go before he finishes.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's helpful information.

Next, I'd like to ask: **Are you currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or have you previously claimed it for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I've been claiming Child Benefit for Alex since he was born. I'm just wondering if I can continue now that he's turned 18, since he's still studying.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's very useful context.

Just to confirm the details: **What is Alex's current living situation - is he living with you full-time, or does he spend time away from home (for example, in student accommodation)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he lives with me full-time at home. He goes to the local college, so he doesn't need to live away or anything like that. He's here with me every day.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I have all the information I need to assess Alex's eligibility.

Based on the details you've provided:

- Alex is 18 years old
- He is in full-time education (A-levels at college)
- He is living with you full-time
- You have been claiming Child Benefit for him since birth

Under UK Child Benefit rules, you can continue to claim Child Benefit for a child over 16 if they are in full-time education or an approved training course. Since Alex meets this criterion, you should be eligible to continue receiving Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

As long as Alex continues his full-time education, you should be able to keep claiming Child Benefit for him. You would need to notify the relevant authorities if his circumstances change (for example, if he stops his studies or moves out).

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
